newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan to raise $280 mln on intl markets - PM.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan to raise $280 mln on intl markets - PM.

text.p: Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Tuesday the former Soviet republic is seeking to raise $280 million on international markets and cut expenses to pay off $500 million in state debts to pensioners.

"In general, the sum needed which we will start paying in July 1997 is about $500 million...we are now on the road to cutting our budget expenses for 1997 -- this is $220 million," Kazhegeldin told diplomats and journalists. "The rest of the money will be borrowed on international markets after receiving a new credit rating," he said.
He said the pensions must be paid off before the year-end.
Kazakhstan issued a debut three-year $200 million Eurobond in December last year, priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. treasury notes.
Moody's gave Kazakhstan a Ba3 sovereign ceiling for long-term foreign currency bonds. Rating agencies IBCA and Standard and Poor's both gave Kazakhstan BB-.
Officials were disappointed by the slightly lower rating than Russia, largely affected by Russia's continued control of the Central Asian state's oil exports.
Plans earlier this year to issue a Samurai bond were scrapped after Kazakh officials said negotiations with Japanese underwriters fell through.
National Bank of Kazakhstan Chairman Uraz Dzhandosov said earlier this month he expected a new credit rating by October, after which the republic would issue another dollar-denominated bond.
